evidence.ref: .warp/claim.py is the fleet's atomic self-dividing claim primitive: a claim file under the git common dir at warp/claims/<unit>.json (shared across worktrees, outside git history) with holder, requirements, and heartbeat. A fresh unit is published by writing the full record to a temp file and os.link-ing it onto the target (link fails if the target exists), so the target is never seen half-written and racing workers get exactly one winner; a live claim is never stolen. A stale, corrupt, or own claim is taken over under a per-unit flock with a re-check under the lock, so concurrent takeovers serialize to one winner and never overwrite a claim that turned fresh. A claim is granted only when the unit's requirements are a subset of the worker's capabilities (free-form tags, so iOS routes to a Mac and GPU work to a GPU box with no hardcoded OS map). heartbeat refreshes, release frees, own re-claim is idempotent. fcntl-based, so Unix-only (Linux and macOS, the fleet's targets).

a selftest block over a temporary claims root drives capability refuse-vs-grant, a BARRIER-synchronized concurrent fresh-unit race (96 threads x 120 rounds, exactly one winner), a barrier-synchronized concurrent stale-takeover (64 threads x 10 rounds, exactly one winner), live-claim-not-stolen, sequential stale reclaim, heartbeat, release, and claimed_units filtering; non-tautological - reverting the atomic os.link publish, removing the takeover lock, or skipping the capability check each turns a threaded assertion red; part of selftest 992 passed, 0 failed

assumptions: Mechanical: the claim/capability/takeover control logic and its real surface (the claim files, os.link, flock) run in the gate over a temp claims root with genuinely threaded races, stdlib only. fcntl makes it Unix-only (acceptable for a Linux/Mac fleet). heartbeat has no fencing lock - a resumed heartbeat by a holder already past the stale threshold can transiently double-hold with a reclaimer and self-resolves on the next heartbeat (worker_id mismatch); this is the inherent TTL-lease limitation and never steals a fresh claim, deferred as a fencing note. This item is the claim mechanics + capability match only; computing the claimable set (Y2) is separate.
rollback: git revert; additive - a new .warp/claim.py, a selftest block, one claim_ledger capability entry (both copies), the WARP-0701 spec, and the PLAN-0007 plan; no protected path; claims live outside git history.
